newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices unchanged, trade dull.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices unchanged, trade dull.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bond prices seesawed back and forth over unchanged in quiet trade at midday on Thursday as brokers waited to see how many of New York City's new bonds would be alloted to them.

"It's kind of hanging up the market, you just don't know whether you have any room," a trader said, adding he expected to learn late this afternoon whether his firm got all the issues it had requested.

The city on Wednesday sold $805 million of tax-exempt bonds, which fetched a top yield of 6.32 percent in 2025, as well as $300 million of taxable issues to European investors, who paid 28 basis points over three-month LIBOR.
Traders said that prices in the secondary market were spotty, as most were unchanged, though some were seen as much as one-eighth of a point up or down.

Activity also was dampened because the lack of new money continued to crimp potential buying interest, a factor that has been dampening municipal bonds for at least a year, and which largely has been attributed to the stock markets' gains.

Mutal funds seemed to be getting a sizable portion of their cash from bonds that have been called, and traders said that as a result, these players were looking for new issues with at least a 10-year maturity and call protection.
"The last thing they want is 2001 or 2002 because then there's no end in sight," a trader said, explaining that large numbers of bonds are expected to be called through 2000.

A sale of $148 million issues by Michigan Building Authority, which fetched a top yield of 5.40 percent in 2010, was expected to do fairly well, in part due to its size and in part because the levels appeared reasonable, a trader said.
Fixed income markets also were bracing for the report on Industrial Production, due out on Friday at 0915 EST.

The data were predicted to have risen 0.6 percent in December, down from a 0.9 percent rise in the previous month, though capacity utilization was expected to have firmed to 83.5 percent from 83.3 percent, according to a Reuters consensus poll of economists.
March municipal bond futures on the Chicago Board of Trade shed 15 ticks to 114-14/32, while U.S. Treasury bond futures, hurt by coroporate hedging, fell 16 ticks to 110-25/32.
This left the MOB spread between the two futures contract at plus 117 ticks.
In the secondary market, Alliance Airport Authority Inc Texas Special Facilities Revenues of April 2021, which pay a 6-3/8 percent coupon, were bid at 100-1/8, up from 99-7/8.
But Florida Ports Financing Community Revenues State Transportation Trust Fund of June 2027, which have a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were bid at 5.82 percent NET, up one basis point.
